title: Kulgam terror attack: Two non-local labourers killed; area cordoned off, search operation launched | Latest updates
content:
• Two non-local labourers, Deepak Ratray (24) and Bopinder (28) from Chhattisgarh, were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in the Kelam area of Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir.
• Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha condemned the Kulgam attack, spoke with Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat, and directed security forces to step up operations.
• The attack occurred during the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, which began on July 3, and less than 10 days after a Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable was shot dead in Anantnag on July 22.

title: IMD sees below-normal August-September rains, reviving inflation fears
content:
• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts India to receive less than 94% of the Long Period Average (LPA) rainfall during the second half (August-September) of the monsoon season.
• Retail inflation accelerated to 4.38% in June, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's 4% midpoint target for the first time since January 2025.
• S&P Global Ratings warned on July 6 that a weak monsoon could push India's inflation to 5.1% in FY27.

title: Eric Trump-backed defense technology company Space-Eyes to go public in $638 million SPAC deal
content:
• Defense technology company Space-Eyes has agreed to go public through a merger with special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) McKinley Acquisition Corp, valuing the combined business at $638 million.
• The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the combined company projected to trade on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "CUAS".
• Eric Trump, a son of President Donald Trump, became the third-largest private investor in the original Space-Eyes and will serve as a strategic adviser to the combined business following the transaction.

title: PM Modi, UK PM Burnham commit to harnessing full potential of mega trade deal for ‘shared prosperity’
content:
• Burnham became the UK prime minister on July 20, succeeding Keir Starmer.
• The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) became operational on July 15.
• The mega trade pact secures zero-duty market access for nearly 99 per cent of India's exports to the UK.

title: Life term for ex-AAP leader Tahir Hussain in Delhi riots case; why city court ruled out death penalty
content:
• Former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain and four other convicts were sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 Delhi riots.
• Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh delivered the verdict, rejecting the prosecution's plea for the death penalty as the case did not qualify as one of the "rarest of rare" cases.
• Tahir Hussain and four other accused were convicted on 13 July for the murder of Ankit Sharma, under various Indian Penal Code (IPC) provisions including Section 302 (murder) and Section 153A (promoting enmity between groups).

title: Extreme heat can erase hundreds of thousands of jobs in India's cities by 2050: World Bank
content:
• New Delhi is projected to lose 266,000 full-time jobs by 2030, rising to 418,000 by 2050 due to extreme heat, while Kolkata could lose 360,000 jobs by 2030 and Mumbai 204,000 jobs by 2030, as per a World Bank report.
• Across South Asia, extreme heat is already costing the equivalent of 31 million full-time jobs each year and could reduce the region's economy by nearly 7% by 2050 if countries fail to adapt.
• India’s sustainable cooling market could be worth $1.6 trillion by 2040, driven by demand for energy-efficient solutions, and heat early warning systems in Indian cities generate about $50 in benefits for every $1 invested.

title: Unfazed by West Asia crisis, fiscal deficit within range at 18.2% in Q1
content:
• The Centre's fiscal deficit in Q1 FY27 (April-June) stood at ₹3.07 lakh crore, which is 18.2% of the full-year target, towards a budgeted fiscal deficit of ₹16.96 lakh crore for FY27.
• The Centre's subsidy bill in Q1 FY27 jumped over 37% year-on-year to ₹1.14 lakh crore, with fertiliser subsidies alone rising to ₹64,667 crore from ₹41,022 crore.
• Capital expenditure for Q1 FY27 remained strong, rising 24% year-on-year to ₹3.40 lakh crore, representing 27.8% of the full-year capex target.

title: PM-KISAN scheme gets 5-year extension and Rs 3.1 lakh crore
content:
• Launched in February 2019, the PM-KISAN scheme provides ₹6,000 a year to eligible landholding farmers in three equal instalments through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.
• Since its launch, the PM-KISAN scheme has disbursed over ₹4.47 lakh crore through 23 instalments.
• The latest instalment of the PM-KISAN scheme transferred over ₹18,984 crore to more than 9.49 crore beneficiaries.

title: A deep dive with Rs 84,084 crore scheme for offshore oil and gas exploration
content:
• The National Offshore Exploration Scheme, named Samudra Manthan, has an outlay of ₹84,084 crore and will be implemented through 2030-31.
• The Samudra Manthan scheme is expected to catalyse reserve accretion of over 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE).
• The government is currently auctioning 18 deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the Open Acreage Licensing Programme, with bids due by September 17.

title: India's forex reserves rise by $6.1 billion to two-month high of $682.35 billion as of July 24
content:
• As of July 24, India's forex reserves rose by $6.1 billion to a two-month high of $682.35 billion.
• India’s forex reserves had scaled a record high of $728.494 billion earlier this year in February.
• Since May 11, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged citizens to conserve foreign exchange by reducing overseas travel, limiting fuel consumption, and avoiding gold purchases for a year.
